name: DGX Spark
facts: A desktop-sized AI computer built around the GB10 superchip.
Delivers up to 1 petaFLOP of AI performance at FP4 precision.
Has 128 GB of unified memory, enough to run AI models of up to 200 billion parameters locally.
This race's commentator, voice and coaching all run live on one DGX Spark at the booth.

name: The GB10 superchip
facts: Combines an Arm-based CPU and a Blackwell-generation GPU in a single package.
CPU and GPU share one pool of 128 GB unified memory, so large AI models fit without copying data between them.
The GB10 powers this race: the language model and the voice models run on it at the same time.

name: 4-bit AI with FP4
facts: FP4 is a 4-bit floating-point number format for running AI models.
It shrinks the memory a model needs while keeping accuracy close to higher precision.
The language model commentating this race runs in a 4-bit format on the GB10.

name: A local language model
facts: The race commentary is written by a 35-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model.
Only about 3 billion of its parameters are active per word, which makes it fast enough for live commentary.
It runs entirely on the device at the booth: no cloud and no internet connection needed.

name: Live text-to-speech
facts: Every commentary line is turned into speech by an open-source text-to-speech model running on the GPU.
A line of speech is generated in about one to two seconds, in English, Dutch or French.
The next line is written and voiced while the current one is still playing.

name: AI race engineering
facts: During the race the game records telemetry for every track section: time lost, off-track moments, crashes and GPUs collected.
After the finish, the language model turns that telemetry into a personal debrief with three concrete tips.
The debrief is streamed word by word as it is generated on the GB10.
